Flashfire

You can't walk. You can't jump. The only way to move is to throw a flaming pearl and teleport to wherever it lands.

It started as a solo build inside a team game jam themed "Teleport." I kept developing it afterwards, adding new levels, tighter aiming, and a limited pearl supply, as a way to actually learn Unity and see how far one mechanic could carry a whole game.

Collect every orb, land every throw, unlock the door. It's rough at the edges on purpose. It's built to keep changing.

Solo dev, post-jam Unity 2D pixel platformer

About

I'm a second-year Game Design and Gameplay Programming student at SAE Institute in Rosebank, South Africa. I like games where the mechanic is the whole pitch: one restriction, pushed until it becomes the entire experience. Most of what's here is unfinished on purpose. I'd rather show the thinking mid-build than a polished demo that stopped growing.

Tools & focus

  • Unity & C#
  • Level design & game feel
  • Rapid prototyping
  • Local multiplayer & input systems

Flashfire
3-person team → solo  |  Unity, C#
2D puzzle-platformer built around a single mechanic: you can't walk or jump, only throw a pearl and teleport to where it lands. Started at a Global Game Jam themed "Teleport" with a 3-person team; continued as a solo project afterward, adding levels and refining the aiming and teleport feel.
Backyard Olympics
Solo  |  Unity, C#
Local multiplayer party game prototype built to learn Unity's new Input System. Designed and coded the RC Boats mode: a bumper-cars-style elimination game with a custom collision-based damage system, HUD health tracking, and player elimination logic.
When You Looked Away
Solo  |  Unity, C#
First-person horror prototype about an entity that only moves when unobserved. Built a state machine to drive its behavior, a gaze-detection system using camera direction and distance checks, and a real-time disguise system that morphs it into nearby furniture.
